about: Country pages for the Veteran Resource Guide (guide.vethomeguard.org/world/). Every number below was read on the official page named in its source, on the date in checked_on. fmp.name: VA Foreign Medical Program (FMP)
fmp.covers: Medically necessary care outside the United States for a VA-rated, service-connected disability, for a condition associated with and held to be aggravating a service-connected disability, or as part of Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E). FMP does not cover care or supplies received in or from the U.S. or U.S. territories.
fmp.letter: Veterans with a VA-rated, service-connected condition can get an FMP benefits letter by signing in to VA.gov and opening Letters from the My VA menu. Providers can use the letter to file claims. If you already paid for care, you can file the claim yourself.
fmp.claims: Claims can be filed online, by email to HAC.FMP@va.gov, or by mail to VHA Office of Integrated Veteran Care, Foreign Medical Program (FMP), PO Box 200, Spring City, PA 19475.
fmp.hours: Monday through Friday, 8:05 a.m. to 6:45 p.m. ET
fmp.claims_source_title: VA.gov: How to file a VA Foreign Medical Program claim

us_canada.note: VA's FMP claims page, updated October 29, 2026, gives 833-930-0816 (TTY: 711; select 3) as the FMP phone line and as the toll-free line from the U.S. and Canada. It replaces 1-877-345-8179 and 303-331-7590 from VA's 2023 FMP Guide, which VA no longer posts.
us_canada.source_title: VA.gov: How to file a VA Foreign Medical Program claim

vcl.name: Veterans Crisis Line from outside the United States

regions.label: Central and South America and the Caribbean (SOUTHCOM)

notes: Each number is assigned to a different U.S. Department of Defense area of responsibility. Off base, dial the number with the U.S. country code; on base, dial DSN 988.
If the number for your region does not work, the Veterans Crisis Line says to try one of the other numbers.
Off base outside the United States, Canada or Mexico, your carrier may charge international rates even for a toll-free number.
Online chat works anywhere with an internet connection. Texting 838255 works from abroad only on a U.S. carrier with an international plan that allows texts to U.S. short codes.

regions.intro: This page gathers what official Japanese and U.S. government pages list for U.S. veterans and military retirees living on Okinawa. For Japan’s national 24-hour crisis line and what we found about veterans agencies in Japan, see the Japan page.

emergency.source_title: GOV.UK travel advice: Japan, getting help
emergency.note: Japan’s national emergency numbers apply on Okinawa.

lines.name: Kokoro no Denwa mental health line (こころの電話相談), Okinawa Prefecture
lines.about: Telephone mental health consultation for people living in Okinawa, run by the Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Mental Health and Welfare Center. The prefecture’s page is in Japanese.
lines.hours: Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, 9 to 11 a.m. and 1 to 4 p.m.; closed Tuesdays, weekends, public holidays, the New Year holidays and Okinawa Memorial Day (Irei no Hi)
lines.partial: Weekday daytime hours only, and closed on Tuesdays. It is not a 24-hour line. For a 24-hour line, see Japan’s national lines on the Japan page; in an emergency, call 119.

lines.name: Okinawa Psychiatric Emergency Medical Information Center (精神科救急医療情報センター)
lines.about: Okinawa Prefecture’s after-hours consultation line for psychiatric emergencies. The prefecture’s page is in Japanese.
lines.hours: Weekdays, 5 p.m. to 9 a.m. the next morning; on days off (休日), 9 a.m. to 9 a.m. the next morning
lines.partial: Nights and days off only. On weekday daytimes, use the Kokoro no Denwa line above. In a life-threatening emergency, call 119.
